learning_outcomes.text: Know, understand and apply ecodesign concepts adapted to new situations for professional development.
Acquire concepts of environmental ethics that allow an in-depth analysis of environmental issues that will affect the engineer in their professional life.
Develop strategies and procedures for solving environmental problems of products and services.
Work in a team and develop knowledge with critical and responsible technical/cultural exchange.
Plan and manage ecodesign projects according to current legislation.
Make an ethical critique of product design.
Create industrial products and analyze their form and function from biomimetics.
Handle software for designing forms inspired by Nature.
Perform a life cycle analysis for an industrial product.

syllabus_topics: Topic ETI-01: Ethical and bioethical bases of ecological ethics.
Topic ETI-02: Ethical concerns in the ecological field: sustainability and ecological justice. Ethical concerns in the technological field.
Topic ETI-03: Paradigms for addressing problems of ecological ethics in engineering: anthropocentrism, biocentrism, and ecofeminism.
Topic LCA-01: Regulations. Ecodesign management systems. ISO 14006.
Topic DIS-01: Business context. Motivating factors.
Topic DIS-04: Biomimetics and fractal geometry.
Topic DIS-06: Product simulation and evaluation.

assessment_methods.method: Active participation in laboratory and classroom practices (EV3)

assessment_rules: To be evaluated, students must attend at least 80% of practical classes (classroom and laboratory). The final grade is calculated as 0.6 * EV1 + 0.3 * EV2 + 0.1 * EV3. If minimum attendance is not met, the student is considered 'not presented' in continuous assessment. If the calculated grade is below 4.0, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. For extraordinary evaluation, students must take a written exam and submit an individual project, with each component weighted at 50%.
